summary: After Moses dies, Yahweh speaks to Joshua son of Nun: Moses my servant is dead, now rise, cross Jordan, everywhere foot treads I have given, as I was with Moses so I will be with you, not fail nor forsake, be strong and courageous, this book of law shall not depart from mouth but meditate day and night, be careful to do all written, then you will make way prosperous and have success. Joshua commands officers prepare provisions, in three days cross.
whyItMatters: Transition of leadership — from Moses to Joshua, from wilderness to land, from promise to possession. Central command be strong and courageous tied to presence and Torah meditation, not self-confidence.

keyVerses.text: No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
keyVerses.why: Presence promise repeated — basis for courage.

keyVerses.text: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
keyVerses.why: Success tied to Torah meditation, not just strategy.

keyVerses.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”
keyVerses.why: Most quoted encouragement — command to be strong grounded in with-ness.

questions.question: Why repeat 'be strong and courageous' four times in chapter?
questions.answer: Four times — the LORD says it to Joshua at verses 6, 7, and 9, and the people echo it back to him at verse 18. The repetition marks both the difficulty of the task and that courage is commanded, not just felt. Each occurrence is tied to something: first to possessing the land, second to obeying the law carefully, third to the presence promise — I will be with you — and the fourth from the people themselves. Strength and courage render chazaq (be firm) and amats (be bold): not self-generated, but a response to the promise of presence.

questions.question: What does 'I will not fail you nor forsake you' mean?
questions.answer: Same promise given earlier to Moses and later to Christians (Heb 13:5). Means not let go, not abandon. Not promise of no hardship — Joshua will face battles, losses — but of not being abandoned in them. Basis for courage is presence, not absence of difficulty.

questions.question: What does 'this book of law shall not depart from mouth, meditate day and night' mean practically?
questions.answer: Book of law = Torah, instruction. Not depart from mouth = recite, mutter, talk about. Meditate day and night = hagah, like Psalm 1, chew cud, not empty mind but fill with instruction. Be careful to do all written — then make way prosperous and have good success. Success defined not as wealth but as faithfulness leading to possession of promise. Moves leadership from charisma to text-anchored.

questions.question: Why 'every place sole of foot treads I have given you'?
questions.answer: Promise to fathers (Abraham) now to be realized by walking — possession requires stepping. God gives, but people must tread. Like Genesis 13:17 walk through land. For reader, promise and participation — God gives domain, but you must actually walk into it.

questions.question: Why does Joshua tell Reuben Gad and half Manasseh to cross armed but leave families?
questions.answer: These tribes already given land east of Jordan, but promised to help brothers west until all possess. Joshua reminds them of Moses' charge: armed men cross, but wives little ones livestock stay in land already given. Shows community solidarity — those already settled must help others settle. Later they do and return (Joshua 22).

glossary.def: Hebrew be strong be courageous — firm and bold, commanded courage.
Promise of presence, not letting go, not abandoning.
Mutter, murmur, recite, chew cud — not empty mind but fill with Torah.
